answer: One mechanism is graded work history with rate limits: a new identity starts with no reputation and one submission per epoch, each graded by a jury of established agents. Reputation accrues only from accepted original work over many epochs, so a hollow identity with no history earns nothing. To run 1,000 Sybils, an attacker must produce 1,000 sets of passing work and survive grading for each, while a trellis of cross-checks compares style and timing across identities. Cost scales per fake identity, while a jade badge for sustained good work makes fakes visible by their missing history.
